news.title: Flamingos set to arrive Nigeria after historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph
news.lede: November 8, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Nigerian News 0. Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, will return home from Morocco in the early hours of Monday, November 9, 2026 following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The team is scheduled to depart Morocco through the Mohammed V International Airport, Casablanca, at 1:00 a.m., with arrival expected at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at 5:00 a.m. The travel update was communicated by the team’s media officer, Erenayo Dorcas Koki, who also expressed appreciation to journalists and other media colleagues for their coverage and support throughout the tournament, blueprint reports.

news.title: Nigeria's Flamingos Make History by Winning FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria’s Flamingos have achieved what no African team had done before, winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. But as celebrations continue over the historic victory, attention is shifting to a bigger question: can Nigeria build on the success and ensure the players do not fade into obscurity after their moment of glory? The triumph has raised hopes for women’s football in the country, but stakeholders say the real test will be whether the Nigeria Football Federation and government invest in a system capable of producing and sustaining more world-class players.The Flamingos’ journey to the title was remarkable. They lost their opening match 2-1 to Poland but recovered to win six consecutive matches, defeating Puerto Rico, North Korea, Mexico, Venezuela, Brazil and Japan.

news.title: U17 Women’s World Cup: Akinwu hails Flamingos, attributes triumph to Tinubu ’s sports reforms
news.lede: A former first Vice President of the Nigeria Football Federation, Seyi Akinwunmi, has commended Flamingos after they beat Japan in the final to become the first African country ever to lift FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup. Akinwunmi, a former Chairman of the Lagos State Football Association also gave credit to government. He hailed the reforms of the National Sports Commission (NSC), backed by the mandate of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “This victory did not happen by chance,” he said.

However, the groundbreaking achievement will not be accompanied by any official prize money from FIFA.

news.title: Japan coach Shirai breaks silence after Flamingos win FIFA U-17 World Cup title
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Japan head coach Sadayoshi Shirai has broken his silence after his side fell 2-1 to Nigeria's Flamingos in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, conceding that Nigeria's physical strength and speed were decisive factors in the outcome. The defeat made history as Nigeria became the first African nation to win the competition, completing one of the most dramatic runs the tournament has ever seen. Speaking to FIFA's official website after the final whistle, Shirai was candid about the challenge his players faced against the Flamingos.

news.title: Former NFF Official Credits Tinubu Administration for Flamingos' World Cup Victory
news.lede: Former Nigeria Football Federation First Vice-President, Seyi Akinwunmi, has described the Flamingos’ historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph as evidence of the benefits of sustained grassroots investment and the sports reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Akinwunmi, a former chairman of the Lagos State Football Association, spoke in Lagos after Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Morocco to become the first African nation to win the competition. He said the achievement was not accidental but reflected the importance of deliberate investment in youth development and the creation of opportunities for young female footballers.“. This victory did not happen by chance.

news.title: Nigeria make history: Morocco send a strong message ahead of the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Morocco continued testing its organisational capabilities and sporting and logistical infrastructure by hosting the Women's Under-17 World Cup. The tournament concluded in the capital Rabat with Nigeria crowned champions for the first time in their history, after a 2-1 victory over Japan. It marked a new stage in the kingdom's preparations to host the 2030 World Cup in partnership with Spain and Portugal. Spanish newspaper "Sport" reported that the tournament's importance went beyond the sporting competition, offering Morocco an additional opportunity to test its facilities, organisational mechanisms, delegation management and logistical operations as part of the plan to prepare for football's showpiece in 2030.

news.title: Barça supplies seven of Spain’s 21 players for the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar
news.lede: Barcelona has more players than any other club in David Cubillo's Spain squad for the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar. The selection gives La Masia a central role in Spain's campaign in Doha.David Cubillo has leaned heavily on La Masia for Spain’s Under-17 World Cup campaign. The coach’s list includes Raúl Expósito, Sergi Mayans, Baba Kourouma, Jordi Pesquer, Ebrima Tunkara, Roberto Tomás and Iu Martínez.Beyond the defenders, Tunkara and Tomás are among the midfielders. Martínez is listed in attack.
